title: Sakalava expansion
description: Under Andriandahifotsy the Sakalava extend their authority along the west coast past the Mangoky river, the rise of the island's great rival to the Merina kingdom.

title: Fort-Dauphin destroyed
description: Antanosy warriors overrun France's colony on Christmas night and murder most of its men; France gives up its first Malagasy venture two years later.

title: Sainte-Marie ceded to France
description: Queen Bety of Betsimisaraka cedes the pirate island of Sainte-Marie to France; the colonists are massacred two years later and France stays away for half a century.

title: Andrianampoinimerina king of Imerina
description: The king of Ambohimanga unites the warring Merina principalities and declares the sea will be the boundary of his rice-field, starting the Merina conquest of Madagascar.

title: Kingdom of Madagascar recognised
description: Under Radama I and a treaty with Britain the inland kingdoms are united and abroad the island becomes known as a single Kingdom of Madagascar.

title: Malagasy alphabet
description: With the Welsh missionary David Jones, Radama I codifies a Latin alphabet for Malagasy, replacing the old sorabe script.

title: Christianity banned
description: Ranavalona I outlaws the practice of Christianity and expels the missionaries, beginning decades of isolation and persecution.

title: Lambert Charter
description: The crown prince secretly signs away sweeping rights to the Frenchman Jean Laborde, a document France later uses to justify intervention.

title: Court turns Anglican
description: Ranavalona II is baptised into the Church of England and makes the Anglican faith the kingdom's official religion.

title: Ranavalona III crowned
description: The young Ranavalona III is crowned, the last monarch of independent Madagascar.

title: First Franco-Hova War ends
description: Peace with France cedes it Antsiranana (Diego Suarez) and a handle on foreign affairs; its meaning is contested from the day it is signed.

title: Britain accepts French protectorate
description: London swaps its claims on Madagascar for French acceptance of British Zanzibar, leaving the Hova kingdom to face France alone.

title: French take Antananarivo
description: A French flying column lands at Mahajanga, marches overland and storms the capital by surprise, ending the second Franco-Hova War.

title: France annexes the island
description: The French parliament votes the annexation of Madagascar; the new regime abolishes slavery, freeing some half a million people, and Gallieni arrives to pacify the island.

title: Rebellion crushed, queen exiled
description: Gallieni puts down the Menalamba rebellion and ships Ranavalona III into exile in Réunion and later Algeria, abolishing the monarchy.

title: Great uprising
description: Peoples and former soldiers across the centre and south rise against the French occupation in the largest revolt since the conquest.

title: Vy Vato Sakelika
description: Malagasy medical students found the secret society Vy Vato Sakelika, the best known of the first nationalist organisations.

title: Battle of Madagascar
description: Fearing the Japanese navy will use the island, British and Commonwealth troops storm the great anchorage of Diego Suarez and take the whole colony from Vichy by November.

title: The 1947 uprising
description: Nationalists attack French posts in the east; the rising spreads and is crushed with a brutality remembered for generations, costing tens of thousands of Malagasy lives.

title: Malagasy Republic
description: The Malagasy Republic is proclaimed as an autonomous state within the French Community.

title: Independence
description: Madagascar becomes fully independent with Philibert Tsiranana as its first president.

title: End of the First Republic
description: Student riots, strikes and a mass protest in the capital force Tsiranana to hand power to General Gabriel Ramanantsoa.

title: Ratsiraka takes power
description: After a year of coups and an assassination, Didier Ratsiraka comes out on top and leads a socialist state for seventeen years.

title: Third Republic
description: After mass protests and an army shooting of demonstrators, a democratic constitution ends Ratsiraka's one-party state.

title: Disputed election crisis
description: Both Marc Ravalomanana and Didier Ratsiraka claim the presidency and the island splits in two for months till the courts and the army side with Ravalomanana.

title: Rajoelina takes power
description: The army hands power to the opposition mayor Andry Rajoelina after months of deadly unrest, a transfer condemned abroad as a coup.

title: Rajoelina returns
description: Rajoelina beats Ravalomanana in the run-off and returns to the presidency, this time by the ballot box.
